column3: The Hebrew names times without the explicit for judgment in BSB.
The Hebrew separately narrates stealing and pasturing a flock; BSB describes pasturing stolen flocks.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the poor hid themselves, without making the oppressors the subject of forcing them into hiding.
The Hebrew leaves these workers unnamed; BSB explicitly supplies the poor.
The Hebrew has vineyard in the singular; BSB has vineyards.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has a rock in the singular and says they embrace it; BSB has rocks and huddling against them.
The Hebrew’s second clause names taking a pledge from the poor without explicitly naming a nursing child, which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew has a sheaf in the singular; BSB has sheaves.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has soul in the singular; BSB has souls.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says at the light; BSB says when daylight is gone.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew shifts from a singular housebreaker to a plural subject; BSB uses plural verbs throughout.
The Hebrew makes morning death-shadow for them; BSB reverses the image, making deep darkness their morning.
The Hebrew has he is light or swift; BSB says they are foam. The last clause has a singular subject.
The Hebrew names waters of snow; BSB describes melting snow.
The Hebrew has him rather than them and describes the worm’s sweetness in him; BSB says the worm feeds on them.
The Hebrew has a singular subject; BSB uses they.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed, while BSB supplies God, and the final subject is singular rather than they.
The Hebrew has him in the singular and an additional clause he leans; BSB gives them a sense of security.
The Hebrew briefly shifts to a singular subject for is no more and has a head of grain in the singular.
The Hebrew has my word in the singular; BSB has my words.
